descriptionChirho: Proper noun designating the fortified city of Azekah (עֲזֵקָה) in the Shephelah of Judah, notably the site near which David slew Goliath and where the Israelites pursued the Philistines (Josh 10:10, 1 Sam 17:1). Multilingual glosses uniformly transliterate the toponym: eng 'Azekah / and-Azekah', spa 'Azeca / y-Azeca', arb 'عَزيقة / و-عَزيقة', kor '아세가 / 그리고-아세가', swa 'Azeka / na-Azeka'. The two clusters differ only by the conjunction waw, a grammatical prefix not a semantic distinction.
